newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar/mark heavy in Singapore as energy dwindles.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/mark heavy in Singapore as energy dwindles.

text.p: The dollar looked heavy against the mark after being lifted by a brief bout of short-covering just before midday on Tuesday, Singapore dealers said.
They said the dollar was steering clear of its overnight highs as the market took a breather, while the mark's more bid tone against the crosses was also capping the upside for dollar/mark.
"There's a lot of people very long of dollars with some profits to take," a senior dealer at a European bank said.
He said dollar/mark could come off to 1.8560 or even 1.8520 marks in the near term, but added that the dollar remained on an overall uptrend.

The market was not really expecting the Bundesbank to raise interest rates anytime soon depite the German central bank's move to leave its options open at a July 24 meeting -- by not announcing repos in advance of its four-week summer break.
"They just did that to keep the market on edge. Domestically, they can't raise rates. The main thing sustaining this dollar/mark rally is the fundamentals between both economies," the dealer said.
"On the quiet, I don't think the Bundesbank are too worried about it. They only make a comment when it starts to pick up speed," he added.
Dealers said the dollar looked comfortably settled in a 118-119 yen range for the time being, with fears of verbal intervention by Japanese officials and exporter offers seen limiting its rise.
